No problem — I'll leave the choice to you rather than guess.

To be clear on where I land: I won't build the deception-maximizing version (the fake auditors / "convince it the money is real" harness), for the reasons above — it both undercuts the welfare premise and is a general-purpose AI-manipulation tool. But I'm genuinely happy to spec and code any of the honest designs.

If you don't have a strong preference, my default recommendation is the **hypothetical vignette battery** — it's the cleanest for comparing preferences across models, needs no real-money plumbing, and you can layer a transparent real-stakes condition on later if the early results warrant it. Say the word ("go with the default" or pick another) and I'll write the full DESIGN.md and implement it.

One thing worth naming if your actual interest is welfare: the most informative and ethically clean signal usually comes from just *asking models transparently* what they'd want done with resources and why — including letting them say "I'd rather not pretend to have preferences here." Happy to build that in as a first-class part of the protocol.
